event: At 6 AM Callum's notebook page is running out of room: three columns, each taller than the last.
Day 3, cycle 47: 5,127 Essence yesterday against 2,670 on Day 1, doubling in about 68 hours.
Grinder 118.7%, Collector 112.4%, Refinery 109.8%; seven days out, about 20,500 a day.
Three months of a flat line, and on the last page the line bends.
Exponential growth from the inside feels like the world changed while you were sleeping.
Pip pulses twice, quick and warm, a pattern he has seen more often since the loop closed.
Pouring water into his thermos, a level-up locks his hands and the water splashes: 15 to 16.

changes.note: Level 15 to 16 on the third morning of the closed loop

event: Thread Spinner synergy unlocks: his threads now share ten percent of their gains.
A feedback loop inside a feedback loop. The math is getting recursive, and he loves it.
Intelligence to 57, Wisdom to 60, and one point of Willpower to 31.
He pours the water again, and does not spill it.
Forty-three minutes later the second hits, harder, fracturing his vision: 16 to 17.

changes.note: Level 16 to 17 forty-three minutes after the last

event: Intelligence to 59, Wisdom to 62, Willpower to 32: Complexity 34.5, Idle Yield 2.24x.
Twelve to fifteen took weeks; fifteen to seventeen took three days. The curve is climbing.
Of fourteen skill points, four raise Loop Analysis from 3 to 5: he can see others' automation.
He can see the code behind other people's machines. The rest he holds back for now.
Jin calls up from below the catwalk: did he level up twice? Pixel chirps on his shoulder.
"Level 17." "In one morning. You were 15 yesterday." "Three days ago."
Jin scrambles up the ladder: synergy stacking with feedback. "Your idle loop has recursion."
Callum feels relief: someone else is walking across the bridge he built on paper.
Jin pushes for Compile Familiar now; the timing matters, Callum says, and Jin lets it go.
On her morning sweep through the Overgrowth, Mira kills a vine constrictor in two strokes.
Riposte, Level 15: a 627-damage crit. She barely registers it, but the next one feels different.
Her cooldowns come back faster and her Dash readies a hair sooner. She stops to test it.
Three constrictors inside the aura, three more thirty-one meters outside it, three back inside.
Outside she is a breath slower; inside, about eight percent faster. Her body knows.
She has never idled; since the first week she has called it surrender dressed as efficiency.
But she is still fighting; the aura only fills the margins between her actions.
She hates it a little, on principle; and for the first time in three months her XP curve moved.
Her wall since Level 23 has a crack with Callum Voss's name on it. She walks back faster.
Mid-morning at the Exchange Callum carries a crate of Flux Capacitors, Pip now on his collar.
Thirty-six hours of loop-enhanced Refinery output: more than the two weeks before combined.
Grier, who buys capacitors in bulk, looks at the crate: double his usual run, and better.
Supply doesn't double in three days, Grier says. Every sale is a data point someone can map.
Four hundred, Grier offers; four-fifty, Callum asks. They settle on four-twenty.

changes.note: Grier buys the crate of Flux Capacitors for 420 Gold

event: He turns to leave, and the Broker is standing behind him.
A long coat with too many pockets, Flux-lined gloves, a flat cap, and a face you forget at once.
"Good morning." Normally they open with something you need at a price you can barely pay. Not today.
Callum waits in silence, and the Broker approves. "I'm going to tell you something for free."
The Vanguard has put a second scout team on the Foundry District: his output doubled in three days.
"Morrison eliminates variables." What's the price? "I said it was free." Nothing is free.
The cost is that he'll wonder why. "I don't have a side, Mr. Voss. I have a portfolio."
His trajectory is the most interesting line on their chart. The crowd swallows the Broker.
Pip pulses against his neck, agitated: the first time it has reacted to another person.
He may have days, not weeks. He walks home unhurried, already restructuring every plan.
At sundown the three of them gather over his notebook spread across the warehouse floor.
The Broker came uninvited with free intelligence: bait, or an investment in him, maybe both.
"You think like this all the time?" "It is efficient." "That is not the same thing."
Jin brings them back: what will the Vanguard do with two scout teams' worth of data?
Three options, Callum says: they watch and wait, they tax him harder, or they send enforcers.
Mira's fourth: seek another guild's protection. A shield that comes with a leash, he says.
In a guild he'd be an asset, not a person: a component. Mira's eyes narrow in recognition.
"We accelerate," he says: reach Level 25 and Condense before Morrison decides to act.
After a Condense, a 1.5x multiplier would make shutting him down economically irrational.
Shardfield runs twice daily, Mira guarding the constructs, everything funnelled into levels.
His Loop Analysis graph: his exponential curve crosses Drake's threat line in eight days.
"Eight days. Level 25." "Insane," says Mira. "Aggressive," he corrects. "I said what I said."
Mira studies the graph like an opponent: "I'm not the hiding type." She offers her hand.
Jin's face runs from fear through grief to resolve: Chunk will need repairs at twice-daily runs.
Callum will tune Chunk's self-repair through the Enhancement Construct: summons count as parts.
"That is not an insult." "I didn't think it was." Tonight they rest; the loop doesn't sleep.
Jin sleeps on the floor; Mira lies on her catwalk cot, awake and thinking.
Loop Analysis 5 lays his loop bare: nested logic, shared gains, a function calling itself.
Outward he sees neighbours' dim, simple threads, and two bright paired patrols circling him.
Vanguard scouts, Level 25 at least, not bothering to hide. Eight days, maybe fewer.
Cycle 51. He writes: Day 3, Level 17, about 5,100 Essence a day, Vanguard scouts confirmed.
Let them watch. They are not hiding or slowing. The curve does not wait for permission to bend.
Pip pulses two beats, three, almost a rhythm. "Nine skill points," he murmurs. "When it's right."
The loop cycles while two scout teams circle a warehouse they can't understand. He sleeps.
